key_idea: A bell toll is exactly a binary decrement when ocelots are 1-bits and the bottom animal is the least significant bit, so the answer is the pile read as a binary number.
sketch: The lowest ocelot becoming a zebra while all zebras below become ocelots is 'subtract one' in binary (lowest 1 becomes 0, trailing 0s become 1s). Hence the number of tolls until no ocelots remain is the value of the N-bit number with the top animal as the most significant bit. O(N). Pitfall: N up to 60 needs a 64-bit integer; simulation is impossible.
